state-of-matter.def: One of the forms matter takes (solid, liquid or gas), set by how closely its particles are packed and how freely they move.

fluid.def: A substance that flows and takes the shape of its container, because its particles can move past one another: a liquid or a gas.

density.def: Mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V, in kg/m³. A property of the material, not of the amount; water is about 1000 kg/m³.

ideal-fluid.def: A model fluid that is incompressible (constant density) and nonviscous (no internal friction), flowing smoothly; the exam's fluids are ideal unless stated.
